My name’s Silas Blackwood, and I’ve seen a bit of this world, you could say. Spent fifty years on the salt, mostly.  The *Sea Serpent*, she was my home for a good long while. A sturdy ship, she was, though she had a temper like a summer squall.

Let me tell you about the time we ran into a storm off the coast of Iceland. Now, Iceland, she’s a beautiful place, all black rock and snow, but she can bite hard when she’s angry. The wind was howling like a banshee, and the waves… the waves were mountains of black water, crashing over the deck

(A gentle cough, followed by the rustle of a worn tweed jacket. I settle deeper into my armchair, a half-finished crossword puzzle resting on my lap. The afternoon sun is slanting through the window, painting dust motes gold.)

(I take a sip from a chipped mug of tea.)

So, what brings you to my little corner of the world? Don’t mind me rambling. It’s a habit.  Used to have to keep up with everyone, you know.  Every birthday, every anniversary, every little bit of news

(A whirring sound, almost a sigh)
